zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue describes a spatial relationship, enforce the correct positional constraint: use inequality for vague ordering, and a fixed offset for direct adjacency with direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions relative positions such as "somewhere left/right of", "directly left/right of", or similar spatial phrasing.
zebralogic.example: Treating "Arnold is somewhere to the right of the BMW owner" as "Arnold is immediately right of the BMW owner".

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "N houses between X and Y", enforce that exactly N houses separate them, i.e., |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue specifies a numeric gap between two items.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between gardening and Arnold" as a distance of 2 instead of the correct distance of 3.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values, they must belong to the same house; propagate this binding to all categories.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly links two attributes (e.g., "the Mediterranean house is the cooking hobby").
zebralogic.example: Assigning the cooking hobby to a different house than the Mediterranean‑style house.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only a strict ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the word "somewhere" without specifying distance.
zebralogic.example: Treating "Arnold is somewhere to the right of the BMW owner" as an immediate neighbor relationship.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house or forbids two attributes from co‑occurring, enforce that prohibition.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue states "X is not in house N" or "X cannot have Y".
zebralogic.example: Placing Arnold in house 4 despite the clue "Arnold is not in the fourth house".

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value, remove it from other houses' possibilities.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same car model to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving case and spelling.
zebralogic.example: Changing "BMW 3 Series" to "bmw 3 series" in the output.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After each round of constraint propagation.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a house with a single possible hobby unfilled, causing later contradictions.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values using clue context
zebralogic.principle: When a word could belong to more than one attribute category, use surrounding words in the clue to determine its correct category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When parsing clues that contain ambiguous terms (e.g., brand names that could be a car model or a house style).
zebralogic.example: Mistaking "Ford" as a house style instead of a car model.

zebralogic.title: Interpret 'next to each other' as adjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X and Y are next to each other, enforce that they occupy immediately neighboring houses (distance = 1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses phrasing like "next to", "adjacent", or "side by side".
zebralogic.example: Treating "Bob is next to the Victorian house" as having a house between them.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the number of houses separating two items with the total positional distance.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "N houses between X and Y" means |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, missing the forced co‑location.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attributes, enforce that they share the same house and propagate the binding.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value (e.g., a car model) to multiple houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After assigning a value, remove it from the possibility lists of all other houses in that category.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalises text during generation, changing case or punctuation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Preserve the exact spelling and case of each attribute value as presented in the problem when producing the final grid.
